name: Move standard-retention consent gating behind cooldown and claim returns
description: Root cause verified on origin/main 08d75f4: POST /retention/recall-test owns consent before processRecallTest, but the service owns the standard/default attempt's active-cooldown and atomic lost-claim exits. Withdrawn consent therefore masks deterministic cooldown results before any recall grader could run.
acceptanceCriteria:
Definition of done (source baseline: origin/main 08d75f4):

1. Consent ordering and externally visible variants
- dont_remember remains deterministic and consent-free: it does not acquire a cooldown claim or call the LLM grader.
- A standard or omitted-attemptMode request with an active cooldown returns the existing cooldown result even when LLM consent is withdrawn; no claim mutation and no grader dispatch occur.
- A fresh standard/default request that loses the atomic cooldown claim returns the existing cooldown result even when consent is withdrawn; no grader dispatch occurs.
- When a standard/default request acquires the exact cooldown claim and consent is withdrawn, it returns the existing consent-denied 403 before the grader runs and attempts to restore that exact claim using the existing optimistic claim guard.
- Failure to restore the acquired claim is captured through the existing non-user-visible error path but does not swallow or replace the consent error; no grader dispatch occurs.
- With active consent after a successful claim, the grader runs exactly once and existing cooldown, grader-unavailable, post-grader CAS, and result-persistence semantics remain unchanged.

2. Boundary coverage
- Update apps/api/src/middleware/metering.coverage.manifest.ts and apps/api/src/middleware/metering.coverage.guard.test.ts so the final recall-test consent owner and ordering are structurally represented; the guard must fail if the standard/default LLM path becomes unclassified or can dispatch without consent. The deterministic dont_remember and cooldown branches remain explicitly represented, and retention metering remains route-owned and unchanged.

3. Regression proof
- Add focused service regressions in apps/api/src/services/retention-data.test.ts for withdrawn-consent active cooldown, atomic lost-claim, acquired-claim restoration, restoration failure preserving the 403, and active-consent grader dispatch. Keep route-level mapping/delegation coverage in apps/api/src/routes/retention.test.ts. The regression test must fail against the production implementation with the fix reverted and pass with the fix present.
- Execute and record the focused red -> green -> production-revert red -> exact-restore green sequence with: DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/mentomate_test pnpm exec jest --config apps/api/jest.config.cjs --runInBand --silent apps/api/src/routes/retention.test.ts apps/api/src/services/retention-data.test.ts apps/api/src/middleware/metering.coverage.guard.test.ts
- Run routed validation with: DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/mentomate_test bash scripts/check-change-class.sh --run --fast

4. Scope and authority
- Expected collision set: apps/api/src/routes/retention.ts, apps/api/src/routes/retention.test.ts, apps/api/src/services/retention-data.ts, apps/api/src/services/retention-data.test.ts, apps/api/src/middleware/metering.coverage.manifest.ts, and apps/api/src/middleware/metering.coverage.guard.test.ts.
- Reuse the existing atomic cooldown claim/release contract. No schema, migration, cooldown duration, retention schedule, mastery/quality policy, prompt/model/provider-routing, metering, or unrelated consent-policy change is authorized. Post-provider CAS behavior is outside this item. If broader authority becomes necessary, stop and obtain a separate ruling/item.
- Acceptance requires an exact-head strict-green Adversarial review because this is a P1 consent/security and concurrency boundary change.
riskImpact: P1 privacy and concurrency defect at the recall-grader boundary. Incorrect ordering can dispatch after withdrawal, hide deterministic cooldown results, strand an acquired claim, or change existing CAS behavior. Existing optimistic claim/release machinery bounds the repair; no schema or retention-policy change is required.
